title: King's Indian Defence
intro: Against 1.d4: let White build a big centre, castle quickly, then attack it. A fighting choice for Black.

lessons.title: The King's Indian set-up
lessons.summary: Fianchetto, castle, then strike at the centre.

steps.text: White opens with 1.d4. In the King's Indian, Black does not fight for the centre at once. First the king gets safe; then Black strikes back.

steps.hint: The knight goes to its best square, f6.

steps.text: Prepare a fianchetto: make room for your bishop on g7.
Put the bishop on its long diagonal.
steps.ifRight: From g7 the bishop aims through the centre.

steps.text: White builds a big centre with 4.e4.
Play d6: it stops e5 and prepares your own ...e5 later.
White played 5.Nf3. Get your king to safety before you fight.
steps.hint: The squares between your king and the h8 rook are empty.
steps.ifWrong: Castle first; the counterattack with ...e5 comes next.
steps.ifRight: Castled. Now Black hits the centre with ...e5 or ...c5.
